text: This is ZivBot, running on my own accounts. No sample data: my real Gmail and my real GitHub, mapped into one FalkorDB graph. Small agents, called Zivs, read that graph and act on it.
Connecting is one click, like in Claude or ChatGPT. Sign in with Google brings in Gmail and Calendar. Sign in with GitHub brings in my repositories, issues and pull requests.
It all lands in FalkorDB, in a graph that is mine alone. Email threads, people, repos, files and issues become nodes and edges. This is the live schema, with full text and vector indexes.
FalkorDB's own algorithms run as tools. PageRank finds the people at the center of my work. Label propagation finds who really works together.
Now a real question. Which emails haven't I replied to? The graph planner answers instantly, straight from my inbox.
Show path opens the exact Cypher behind the answer, with row counts and timings. No black box.
And I can pick the model, per chat. Here it's Codex, on my own ChatGPT subscription. It calls ZivBot's graph tools over MCP, and its Cypher still shows up under the answer.
Or Claude, on my Claude plan. Same graph, same tools. Who works with me on Loom? It follows the contributor edges and answers.
Zivs act, but only with my approval. Draft a reply to Nivesh. The draft waits right here. Nothing is sent until I approve it, and then it goes out through my real Gmail.
Zivs are cheap to make. I add Ledger, a finance Ziv, from a template. They all share one graph memory, and they message each other.
Now my phone. This QR code opens an end to end encrypted channel to this laptop, over Supabase Realtime. It works from any network, as long as the laptop is on.
On the iPhone, it's the same Zivs and the same graph, answering from my laptop, wherever I am.
And every graph tool is also an MCP server. Here a real Codex session calls ZivBot's triage tool on my graph. ZivBot: agents that act on your real data, with FalkorDB at the center.
